paper.title_en: IR/UV mixing from higher-order interactions in a Scalar Field
paper.abstract_en: The observed vacuum energy lies far below the usual quantum-field-theoretic estimate. We construct a preferred-frame reduced scalar Hamiltonian in which a nonlocal quartic field derivative interaction produces a wavevector dependence proportional to $|\vec k|^8$ for modes below a smoothly defined scale. Within the quartic oscillator regime, the ground-state energy and excitation gaps are $\propto |\vec k|^{8/3}$. The preferred frame is characterized by a timelike clock-field background. The Planck energy is reached at a substantially smaller value of the spatial wavevector due to its supra-linear mode-energy dependence. The proposed interaction is instantaneous in the preferred frame and yields a Hamiltonian bounded below. Normalizing the peak of the ground-state energy to the Planck scale, together with Cohen-Kaplan-Nelson (CKN) saturation, applied as a matching recipe rather than as an {\it {ab initio}} calculation, fixes the cutoff scale at $k_G\sim k_{Pl}^{1/3}k_{box}^{2/3}$. Modes above the smooth cutoff scale retain their ordinary scalar dynamics. We assume that the interaction-induced ground-state energy shift gravitates, as do other contributions. CKN saturation is imposed on the total vacuum energy, comprising this shift and the other vacuum contributions. Identifying the inferred infrared scale phenomenologically with the cosmic event horizon reproduces the holographic-dark-energy relation $ρ_{vac}\propto\frac{M_{Pl}^2}{R_h^2}$, provided the coupling tracks the horizon; the resulting holographic fluid has $w_0\simeq-0.89$.
